learn.title: Data that survives
learn.body: Variables vanish when the program ends. A file keeps data on disk. In C you open a file with `fopen`, which returns a `FILE *`: a pointer to a handle that the library uses to track your position in the file. When you are done you call `fclose`.

learn.title: The mode string
learn.body: `fopen(path, mode)` needs a mode. `"r"` reads and needs the file to exist. `"w"` writes and empties an existing file, or creates it. `"a"` appends to the end. Be careful: `"w"` on a file you wanted to keep deletes its contents.

learn.title: Always check for NULL
learn.body: If `fopen` fails, it returns `NULL`. It may fail because the folder or file does not exist, or you lack permission. This program prints `cannot open`.

learn.title: The usual flow
learn.body: Every file program follows the same steps.
steps: `fclose` it, which also saves pending data

questions.explanation: Always test for `NULL` before using the pointer.
